Dye that colours cells so the pathologist can see them, like H&E or the Gram stain.
Fluid of plasma and cells carrying oxygen and nutrients.
Crossbar linking the two branches of an H-shaped fissure on the brain surface.
Crush syndrome: muscle trapped under rubble for hours breaks down, and freeing it floods the blood with potassium and myoglobin. Today is World Tsunami Awareness Day.
Pain shooting from the buttock down the back of the leg, from an irritated sciatic nerve (often a bulging lumbar disc). Most cases settle on their own within weeks to a few months.
Old unit of radioactivity, named after Marie and Pierre. Marie was born on this day in 1867.
Fleeting or transient, as in amaurosis fugax: brief monocular vision loss.
A test of a treatment in people. The randomised controlled trial is the gold standard. Carl Sagan, born today, would ask to see one.
Bones of the head that protect the brain.
Tissue moved from one place to another. WWI surgeon Harold Gillies rebuilt soldiers’ faces with skin grafts and flaps.
Confined to one lobe, like classic pneumococcal pneumonia.
Posterior pituitary hormone that drives labour contractions and milk let-down. Nicknamed the ‘cuddle hormone’. Happy World Kindness Day.
Cluster of pancreatic cells, beta cells included, that makes insulin.
Ridge or furrow joining two structures, e.g. the jugum sphenoidale of the skull base.
Plant roughage your gut can’t digest. Legumes, wholegrains and veg are full of it, one reason the Mediterranean diet works so well.
Pap ___: the old cervical screening test. Australia swapped it for an HPV test in 2017.
Short for Staphylococcus. The S in MRSA.
The intestines, especially the large intestine.
Organ grown during pregnancy that swaps oxygen, nutrients and waste between parent and baby through the umbilical cord. Delivered after the baby: the afterbirth.

Surgery cutting connections to the brain’s frontal lobes. Egas Moniz won the 1949 Nobel Prize for it; it is now seen as one of medicine’s worst wrong turns. Alfred Nobel signed his will on this day in 1895.
